headline: Hot jobs report revives hike fears; tone tilts toward fear
body: Markets are closed today for Labor Day, so the tape carries over from Friday's close, which came in soft: the S&P 500 slipped 0.4% to 7,718.60, the Nasdaq eased 0.3% to 26,506.99, and the Dow fell 0.5% (-271.86 points) to 53,414.25. The trigger was the August jobs report — nonfarm payrolls up 162,000 versus roughly 53,000 expected, unemployment steady at 4.1% — a beat that traders read as fuel for the Fed's hawks rather than good news. Fed funds futures now imply something like a 60-65% chance of a rate hike at the September 16 meeting, up sharply from the mid-30s a week earlier, after Chair Kevin Warsh's Jackson Hole speech sharpened his inflation warnings. Treasury yields moved higher on the repricing, and a post-earnings plunge in Lululemon added to the defensive undertone heading into the long weekend.

The CNN Fear & Greed Index has slid to 43 — fear territory — consistent with a hawkish repricing rather than any single shock. There's also an unusual political wrinkle: Vice President Vance has publicly pushed for lower rates even as Trump's own pick to lead the Fed leans toward tightening, a split markets are still digesting rather than resolving. Retail chatter offered less of a clean signal than the macro story today; StockTwits activity skewed toward AI and data-center names — Salesforce, CrowdStrike, Nvidia, and Vertiv — on earnings and buildout optimism, suggesting pockets of enthusiasm concentrated in a handful of tech themes rather than a broad risk-on mood. On balance, the read leans more on price action and Fed positioning than on any coherent wave of social sentiment.
